fig1_occupation_numbers.svg: Mean occupation $\langle n\rangle$ vs $(\varepsilon-\mu)/kT$ from bose_einstein, fermi_dirac and maxwell_boltzmann. Bosons (orange) diverge as $\varepsilon\to\mu^+$; fermions (blue) obey the Pauli ceiling $\langle n\rangle\le1$ and pass through $\frac{1}{2}$ at $\varepsilon=\mu$; all three merge onto the classical $e^{-x}$ once $\varepsilon-\mu\gg kT$.
fig2_planck_spectrum.svg: Planck spectral energy density $u(\omega)$ from planck_energy_density at 4000 and 5778 K: hotter means a taller spectrum whose peak shifts up as $\hbar\omega_\mathrm{max}=2.82\,kT$ (Wien, dots from wien_peak_x). The classical Rayleigh-Jeans law (dashed, rayleigh_jeans) tracks it at low $\omega$ but runs off as $\omega^2$ -- the ultraviolet catastrophe the quantum $1/(e^{x}-1)$ cuts off.
